Two-voice Socratic lesson: lesson_script (dialogue mode) → lesson_slides → lesson_narrate (two distinct kokoro voices) → lesson_record → lesson_compile, run to `completed`. The FIRST live exercise of two-voice lesson narration. Lessons are child-only (a top-level `lesson` project is rejected), so the parent is a minimal course used only as a container: `run_target.child_index:0` makes the validator run the LESSON child's own deliverable instead of the course deliverable, exposing the lesson blueprint's stages to `expect_stage_assertions`. `brief.dialogue.enabled` on the child turns on the Socratic prompt (student asks / instructor answers); the validator's distinct_count check on `lesson_script.paragraphs[].speaker` proves the live LLM + deterministic role re-derivation produced BOTH a student and an instructor turn (green alone would not prove the script went two-voice), and lesson_narrate clips prove the dual-voice synth ran. Per-line voice→speaker mapping is deterministic and covered by unit tests. `config_overrides.ai_image_gen:false` SUPPRESSES the lesson's default per-slide image generation (run_setup adds it for lessons unless an override is present) so this scenario does NOT depend on the GPU image-gen backend (mini1) — ai_image_gen StageSkips, lesson_record renders title+bullets slides without hero images (it is explicitly tolerant of a skipped ai_image_gen), and the run still reaches `completed`. This isolates the two-voice signal from image-gen flakiness; the full lesson render incl. images is covered by course_happy_path. duration_minutes:2 keeps narrate to a handful of TTS calls.

FLOOR PINNED, NOT RE-SIZED (recorded 2026-09-03). `lesson_script paragraphs[].speaker >= 2` looks fragile blueprint-wide -- MEASURED over a 90-day window of completed `stage_outputs` the distinct speaker count is min 0 (n=44) -- but that minimum is single-voice lessons, which do not set dialogue mode and legitimately carry one speaker or none. Here two speakers are pinned by the INPUT: `lessons[0].brief.dialogue.enabled` is true, which is exactly the switch that makes lesson_script emit a two-speaker Socratic script, and the assertion is the proof that switch was honoured. Lowering it would leave the scenario named 'two voice' unable to tell a two-voice lesson from a one-voice one. tests/test_e2e_scenario_contracts.py now requires any `paragraphs[].speaker >= 2` floor to be backed by `dialogue.enabled: true` on the targeted lesson, so silently turning dialogue off reds in CI rather than quietly reddening the nightly.
